utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: At 10 CFU, something is amiss and the operator needs to look for the culprit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: A threshold by itself prevents nothing, though.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: What reduced elevator results from repeat systems 86% in the city of Vancouver in four years was the follow-up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: We tracked the repeated systems and focused our efforts there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: They drove two-thirds of the citywide decline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: We didn't send an inspector to every number.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: We sent one when the numbers repeated, and we sent them to look at the system, not just the water result.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: In Vancouver, it was nearly always a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: mechanical or an operator fault.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: That's prevention, not reaction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: Finding out at 1000 CFU or after the outbreak versus knowing the sample was taken and reported.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: You can't act on the number you never see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: So here I'm telling you that regulation works, Vancouver's program works, and we have the data to prove it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: In New York City, when a child's blood lead comes back at 3.5, you find the lead and the owner is ordered to remove it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: It used to be 15, a level where the damage is already irreversible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: 10 is a 3.5 of coolant towers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: Find the fault and fix it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: You build the program around the system, not just the coolant tower, and your efforts will be rewarded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We really appreciate your testimony and you agreeing to do that today.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And we'll be in contact with you, too, because we want to do something with this.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip White
utterances.text: Thanks.

chapters.summary: Jan Horn, president of the Cooling Technology Institute, opposes lowering the Legionella reporting threshold to 10 CFU/mL. He argues policy should follow demonstrated public health benefits, says major technical guidance emphasizes comprehensive water management over a single low test result, and offers CTI as a technical resource.
chapters.title: Jan Horn of Cooling Technology Institute opposes 10 CFU Legionella threshold

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Next is Ian Horn.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ian Horn.

utterances.text: Yes, we can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: Yes, thank you so much.

utterances.text: We have submitted a written testimony along with our application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: I'm going to present to you a very short summary of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: Good morning, Chairperson Shulman and members of the City Council Health Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: My name is Jan Horn, and I'm the president of the Cooling Technology Institute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: I come before you today in opposition of proposed legislation to amend New York City's reporting requirements for Legionella test results.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: We ask that you do not lower the Legionella reporting threshold to 10 CFU per milliliter as proposed by this bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: I am also offering our services as a technical resource on the topic of Legionella control and prevention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: We are here at your service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: CTI is an independent nonprofit organization dedicated to advocating and promoting for the benefit of the public safe use of all environmentally responsible and energy efficient cooling technologies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: Our organization is responsible for drafting many internationally recognized standards and guidelines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: We appreciate the Council's commitment to protecting New Yorkers from Legionnaires disease and we share that objective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: However, we believe that policy decisions should be based on demonstrated public health benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: Major technical guidance documents, including CTI Guideline 159, ASHRAE Standard 188, and ASHRAE Guideline 12, emphasize comprehensive water management practices in investigation of system conditions rather than the reliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: on one single low Legionella test result.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: While Legionella concentrations are one important indicator of system performance, no single concentration has been demonstrated to reliably predict human illness across all building types, operating conditions, and exposed populations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: To our knowledge, peer-reviewed research has not demonstrated that reducing the reporting threshold to 10 CFU improves Legionnaires'disease prevention or public health outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: For that reason, CTI strongly encourages continued emphasis on robust water management programs, timely investigation of elevated results, epidemiology-guided outbreak investigations, and operator training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: CTI also believes Legionnaires'disease investigations are most effective when they evaluate all potential environmental sources, including entire building water systems, as well as all incoming potable water systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: supplies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: In conclusion, CTI asks that you do not lower the recording detection limit to 10 CFU, and we are available to you as a technical resource on this topic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jan Horn
utterances.text: I thank you for your time.

summary: Committee on Health held an oversight hearing on food service establishment inspections in New York City and considered several related local laws on inspection documentation, food protection certificates, children's meals, tobacco bars, and Legionella reporting.

DOHMH Deputy Commissioner Corinne Schiff testified on restaurant grading, inspection capacity, and the department's positions on Intro 189, Intro 908, Intro 1124, Intro 405, Intro 947, and Intro 1094, followed by extensive Council Q&A.

Public testimony included Local 768 on inspector staffing and Intro 189, health advocates on children's meals and tobacco bars, and supporters and opponents of lowering the Legionella reporting threshold to 10 CFU/mL.
